headline: Palace Says ₱180-Million Regional Evacuation Funds Are for Permanent Disaster Shelters
seoTitle: Palace Clarifies ₱180M Regional Evacuation Funds | FMB News
seoDescription: Malacañang says the ₱180-million regional evacuation allocations are intended for permanent disaster infrastructure designed to reduce reliance on classrooms as shelters.
deck: Malacañang says the allocations are intended for permanent evacuation infrastructure, including facilities designed to reduce the use of classrooms as temporary shelters.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Malacañang said a ₱180-million allocation per administrative region is intended for permanent evacuation-center infrastructure, responding to questions over the use of disaster-related public funds.

According to the approved FMB News morning brief, the Palace said the program is meant to build climate-resilient shelters and reduce the long-standing practice of using public-school classrooms as evacuation sites during typhoons, floods and other emergencies.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Using classrooms as temporary shelters can prolong disruptions to schooling after a disaster. Dedicated evacuation centers are intended to separate emergency shelter operations from regular school functions and provide facilities designed specifically for displaced families.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The issue combines disaster preparedness with public-spending accountability. Clear project locations, procurement records, engineering standards and implementation timelines will be important for assessing whether the allocations translate into usable facilities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for detailed implementing documents identifying project sites, procurement schedules, construction milestones and audit records for the regional allocations.
